messages:
morgan: Quick heads-up — CI perf alert for hosted-inference: 95th latency up ~8% on small-request workload since yesterday. profiler points at host-side work (tokenization + request parse) and gRPC writev path.

kai: ugh. which path in the flame? host or proxy? paste profiler snippet? :eyes:

morgan: host-side. coming from the new kernel-selection change + tiny-request burst affecting batching heuristics. snippet below (top 5 ms buckets):
```
host_tokenize: 32%
parse_and_frame: 21%
grpc_writev_smallwrites: 18%
kvcache_lookup: 9%
decode_prep: 7%
```

anya: that grpc_writev item rings a bell — we saw smallwrite headroom regress after the coalesce heuristics tweak last week. could be more syscalls due to uncoalesced frames.

samir: also note kvcache jump — I've seen thrash when token boundaries change: partial tokens produce different cache keys so hit rate drops. any change to tokenization splitting rules landed?

morgan: no direct tokenizer change in this rollout, but kernel selector now prefers a shorter-seq kernel which bakes in different chunk boundaries for pre-tokenized segments. that can shift token offsets.

lucas: interesting. kernel selection -> different sequence chunking -> token boundary shift -> KV cache misses -> longer host preproc? nasty chain. can we reproduce with a synthetic burst?

morgan: yes, running a microbenchmark now (repro script at https://go/internal/perf/repro/4897). local run shows kvcache hit drop ~12% correlated with more parse calls.

kai: short-term mitigation: revert writev coalesce tweak? or force coalescing for small requests (threshold up). can do a quick canary.

anya: alternative: move tokenization earlier into edge (sidecar) so host gets pre-tokenized frames and consistent keys. that reduces host CPU but trades network bytes and complexity.

samir: we should also try a cache-key normalization: base keys on semantic token ids rather than byte offsets so small boundary shifts don't bust hits. might be more invasive.

morgan: agreed on multiple experiments. plan: 1) canary revert grpc smallwrite change (kai) 2) run kernel-selector rollback to previous heuristic on canary (lucas) 3) synthetic reproducer + kvkey-normalization sim (samir + anya). I'll coordinate.

kai: starting canary rollback now. deploy-bot: deploy request for eng-runtime/canary -> staging-a (rollout-id 5721).

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: eng-runtime/canary -> staging-a. status: in-progress.

lucas: while that's running, I pushed an instrumented build that tags token boundaries in telemetry (header x-token-boundary). will surface delta in traces.

morgan: awesome — once canary is up we'll collect 30m of traffic and compare kv hitrate + tail latency. if revert fixes it, we ship rollback. if not, proceed to kernel rollback.

anya: small note: batching heuristic parameters to vary: max_batch_ms, max_batch_tokens, and small_write_coalesce_threshold. we'll grid search on canary traffic. keep an eye on cost impact.

samir: I'll prototype kvkey-normalization locally (script in the repro dir). if it reduces miss rate in the sim we can evaluate complexity.

morgan: thanks team. filing short postmortem stub: https://docs.redwood/infra/perf/4897-inc — I'll update after data. :thumbsup:

kai: canary green so far (10m). early numbers: 95p latency down ~6%, kvcache hit +9%. will leave rolling and collect 30m.

morgan: sweet. leave the trace tag on — we'll convo again after 30m.

lucas: +1. good job catching the cascade.

samir: noted follow-ups for longer-term: key normalization + consider token-pool reuse to amortize tokenization cost.

anya: also document kernel-selector invariants so sequence-chunking changes are visible to cache team next time.

morgan: agreed. closing for now, will summarize in the postmortem.
